title.rendered: Thanks Be to God for His Indescribable Gift: The Gift Is Christ | The Thankful Heart, Day 14

excerpt.rendered: 2 Corinthians 9:15 thanks God for His indescribable gift. Day 14 of The Thankful Heart closes the series and leads into Advent: the Gift is Christ.

content.rendered:
Paul ran out of words. After chapters about giving and generosity, he lifted his eyes to the greatest Gift of all and simply said: thanks be to God. Some gifts are too big to describe. This one has a name: Jesus.

The Gospel For Today | Saturday, November 28, 2026 | The Thankful Heart, Day 14

Today’s Scripture

“Thanks be to God for His indescribable gift!”
2 Corinthians 9:15 (NKJV)

“For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life.”
John 3:16 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Fourteen days ago we stood at the gate of Psalm 100 and entered with thanksgiving. Since then we have learned to give thanks in everything with Paul, to turn back with the one healed leper, to thank the Father before the miracle at Lazarus’ tomb, to give thanks over five loaves, to let peace rule, to grow deep roots, to offer the sacrifice of praise, to sing at midnight, to remember His benefits, to stand in His victory, to sing the chorus of His mercy, and to thank God for the people He has given us. Every one of those thanksgivings leads back to one place.

In 2 Corinthians 8 and 9, Paul has been encouraging the church to give generously to believers in need. He talks about sowing and reaping, about cheerful giving, about God who supplies seed to the sower. Then, at the very end, his thoughts rise past every human gift to the Gift behind them all. “Thanks be to God for His indescribable gift!” Earlier in the same section he had already named it: you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, yet for your sakes He became poor (2 Corinthians 8:9).

The word translated “indescribable” is the Greek anekdiēgētos (ἀνεκδιήγητος), found only here in the whole New Testament. In English, indescribable is often used loosely for a fine meal or a beautiful view, but anekdiēgētos is far stronger: it means inexpressible, something that cannot be fully told. Paul has just spent two chapters describing generous giving in careful detail, and now he says this Gift cannot be told at all. And that is exactly right. How do you describe the eternal Son of God becoming a baby in Bethlehem? How do you describe the sinless One taking our sin, the Life of the world entering death, the empty tomb, the Spirit poured out, the door to the Father thrown open forever? Every word falls short. “For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son.” The love is in the giving, and the Gift is Christ.

Sunday, November 29, is the first Sunday of Advent. Churches around the world, from Lagos to London, Manila to Sao Paulo, will light the first candle and begin the season of waiting for Christmas. The Thankful Heart has been preparing us for exactly this. Advent is not about getting ready to receive something new. It is about learning again to give thanks for the Gift already given, and to look with joy for His return.

So as the series closes, let your thanks gather into one great word. Thank Him for His gates and His goodness, for His victory and His mercy, for the people and the provision. And then thank Him for the One who holds all of it together: Jesus, the indescribable Gift. Carry that thankful heart into Advent, and every candle you light will shine a little brighter.

What the Thankful Heart Was Really About

Thanksgiving is a response, not a payment. We give thanks because the gate is already open in Christ.

Thanksgiving works in every season. In plenty and in want, before the miracle and at midnight, His mercy endures.

Thanksgiving always leads to Jesus. Every gift points back to the indescribable Gift, and Advent begins with Him.

Declaration

Thanks be to God for His indescribable gift (2 Corinthians 9:15)! Father, I thank You that You so loved the world that You gave Your only begotten Son, and that because I believe in Him I have everlasting life (John 3:16). I thank You that though Jesus was rich, for my sake He became poor, that through His poverty I might become rich (2 Corinthians 8:9). I thank You that Your presence, Your peace, Your grace and Your victory are already mine in Him. I carry a thankful heart into Advent, rejoicing in the Gift You have already given. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
